Subject: Rewriting our discount ladder (MediCore)

Hi Hannah,

Thanks for the call this morning — appreciate you walking through the hosted API pricing. Our procurement team wants to move away from a slab (volume bands) structure and trend toward marginal per-token discounts so our finance team can forecast an effective blended rate more predictably across multi-region usage.

Two asks to unblock internal approvals: 1) a worked example that shows blended effective rate at 3 volume points (5M, 50M, 250M tokens/month) for both your slab proposal and a marginal-breakpoint approach; 2) language we can share with legal that locks the breakpoints for the first 6 months and defines a rollback/true-up if usage dips below committed bands.

Can you send a short packet that includes math + a simple rollback playbook? Preferably by EOD tomorrow — Legal is running a sprint.

Best,
Alicia

Hi all,

Attached is a spreadsheet with three tabs: 1) Assumptions/model mix (your uploaded mix + our default), 2) Slab (step) calculation with blended effective rates, 3) Marginal breakpoint calculation and comparison. Highlights:
- At 5M tokens: slab and marginal end up nearly identical (difference < 0.8%);
- At 50M tokens: marginal gives a ~4.6% better blended effective rate for the same total spend;
- At 250M tokens: marginal yields ~7.9% better blended effective at our proposed breakpoints.

I added two clawback scenarios in the True-up tab: 6% and 10% holdback applied to the delta between committed monthly bands and actual usage for any month in the first 3 months post-commit. The model also simulates a 3-month grace period before clawback.

Link to sheet (view): https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1a2b3c-medicoresheet (you should have access)

Attachments: medicore_requested_model_mix.xlsx (your upload), redwood_worked_examples_medicore.xlsx (our calculations).

Let me know if you want the marginal breakpoints shifted tighter (more breakpoints at low usage) — that reduces downside at the expensive end but compresses savings at scale.

Hannah / Dev — thanks for the fast turnaround. I scanned the sheet and a couple items we need clarified before Legal will proceed:

1) Effective rate target: MediCore leadership wants weighted effective $/1k tokens at or below $0.085 at 50M tokens/month (our target after platform discounts). Can you highlight how to hit that via marginal breakpoints vs a slab?
2) Breakpoint freeze period: Legal wants the breakpoints and marginal rates fixed for the first 6 months, with an explicit re-evaluation window at month 6 and 12. Any changes prior to month 6 should require a mutual written agreement.
3) Rollback language: please give sample contract language for a fallback where if usage drops below 70% of committed band for any month during the first 3 months, Redwood will revert the effective rate to the prior slab for that month and true-up at quarter end.

If you can mark these in the PDF we can pass to legal quickly.

Thanks,
Samir

Subject: Re: Rewriting our discount ladder (MediCore) — proposed contract snippets

Alicia / Samir — following up with clean contract snippets and the recommended operational guardrails. Pasting below so Legal can copy straight into the SOW/Order Form: 

1) Breakpoint Fix: "The parties agree that the pricing breakpoints and corresponding per-token marginal rates set forth in Exhibit A shall remain fixed for an initial period of six (6) months following the Effective Date. Any adjustments to such breakpoints during that period require written mutual agreement executed by authorized representatives of both parties."

2) Rollback & True-up: "If during the first three (3) months following a monthly Commitment Start Date, Customer's measured usage for any given month is less than seventy percent (70%) of the committed band for that month, Redwood may temporarily revert the per-token pricing for that month to the prior slab rates. Any amounts owed due to such reversion will be calculated and invoiced as a true-up at the end of the subsequent calendar quarter, subject to audit rights as set forth in Section X."

3) Holdback/Clawback Example (operational): "A holdback equal to six percent (6%) of monthly invoice amount will be retained for the first three calendar months following activation of committed capacity. Holdback amounts will be reconciled at the end of the third month; if Customer meets or exceeds the committed run-rate, holdback will be returned to Customer as a credit. If Customer falls short, holdback will be applied to outstanding invoiced true-up amounts."

Operational notes: we recommend a 3-month grace period before clawback starts and a single true-up at quarter end to minimize churn on billing. We can also add a cap to total clawback exposure (e.g., not to exceed 15% of the committed monthly spend) if that helps legal.

If this looks good, Hannah — I'll prepare a short redlined Exhibit A and a 1-page annotated explanation for Legal.

Thanks,
Rishi
